youtube.title: He Won A 544 Mile Race By Not Sleeping (True Story) 🏃
youtube.description:
In 1983, Cliff Young, a 61-year-old farmer from Beech Forest, Victoria, turned up to the Sydney to Melbourne Ultramarathon, about 875 km (544 miles), in overalls and work boots. The other runners were world-class athletes, and he shuffled along far behind them on the first day.

The other runners slept about six hours a night. He woke up by mistake at 2 a.m., started running again, shuffled past the others while they slept and took the lead. From then on he barely stopped: he had spent days at a time rounding up sheep on his farm.

He finished in 5 days, 15 hours and 4 minutes, 10 hours ahead of second place and almost two days faster than the previous record for the run. Then he gave most of his A$10,000 prize to the other runners.

Could YOU keep going without sleep? 👇
